comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up on [the previous review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12978#issuecomment-5805040422) and [the author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12978#issuecomment-5805791556), checked at `13597029b25a`.

**Outcome:** most of the previous findings are fixed in this commit. Two are still present: the default keybindings bypass the new commands, and global switching moves focus off the current monitor. Hotplug is now handled in Lua, but the bash helpers still act on disconnected monitors, and with allocation now working this resets the desktop to slot 1 on reload. New in this revision: the bar can miss the first enable, the move helper's fallback is unreachable, workspace IDs above 99 stop syncing, and the new `monitor-base-test.sh` fails.

| Previous finding | Status at `13597029b25a` |
|---|---|
| Allocator never allocates | **Resolved.** Isolated run with a synthetic `hyprctl`: `sync` prints `eDP-1 0`, `HDMI-A-1 10` (empty at `caff3e03ef34`) |
| Move helper reads numeric monitor ID | **Resolved.** Same setup, focused `HDMI-A-1`, slot 2: moves to `"12"` (was `"2"`) |
| Bar global flag can never become true | **Resolved**, with a first-enable gap (see below). Source-derived |
| Bar excludes secondary monitors' ranges | **Resolved** through the working flag. Source-derived |
| Config reload stall | **Resolved.** No `io.popen` or synchronous IPC during config evaluation |
| Missing `omarchy:summary=` metadata | **Resolved.** `test/cli` passes at this head |
| Stale `config/hypr/toggles/workspace-global.lua` | **Resolved.** Removed |
| Hotplug not picked up until reload | **Partly resolved.** Lua handles `monitor.added`/`monitor.removed`; the bash helpers still use disconnected monitors (see below) |
| Default keybindings bypass the new commands | **Still present** (see below) |
| Focus and pointer move off the current monitor | **Still present** (see below) |

**Verified:** local mode (toggle off) is unchanged from base in the bar and both entry commands. The earlier toggle-path and missing-helper findings stay resolved.

On two points in the reply: the stdin/heredoc allocator and the `StandardPaths`/`FileView.exists` bar code were both present at the previously reviewed head `caff3e03ef34`. This commit replaced them. Config evaluation still runs `mkdir -p` and two backgrounded helpers, but nothing waits on Hyprland IPC.

## Still present

### Global switching still moves focus off the current monitor

The reply says the focused monitor is now processed last. [`omarchy-hyprland-workspace-global-switch`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/13597029b25a90b70623ce82c1cc8aca9bdbad95/bin/omarchy-hyprland-workspace-global-switch#L46-L58) changed only in its header metadata in this commit. It still dispatches every base in ascending order and never reads or restores the focused monitor. No `focus({ monitor })` call exists in the tree. The [Lua hook](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/13597029b25a90b70623ce82c1cc8aca9bdbad95/default/hypr/toggles/workspace-global.lua#L251-L259) dispatches `focus({ workspace })` for each other monitor. In Hyprland 0.56.2 (`ConfigActions.cpp`, `changeWorkspace`), that focuses the workspace's owner monitor and warps the pointer.

```text
Modelled with a stub Hyprland Lua API, not a native run:
SUPER+2 on eDP-1 (2 monitors)       -> focus ends on HDMI-A-1
SUPER+2 on HDMI-A-1 (3 monitors)    -> focus ends on DP-2
switch helper from HDMI-A-1         -> focus ends on the highest-base monitor
```

**Impact:** after switching slots, keyboard focus and the cursor can end on a different monitor from the one in use.

**Suggested change:** dispatch the originating monitor last in both the helper and the hook, or refocus it with `focus({ monitor = ... })` after syncing.

### Default keybindings still bypass the new commands

[`default/hypr/bindings/tiling.lua`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/13597029b25a90b70623ce82c1cc8aca9bdbad95/default/hypr/bindings/tiling.lua#L21-L25) is unchanged. The PR contains no `install.sh`, installer, migration or documentation change for bindings, so the reply's automatic keybinding install is not part of this PR.

**Impact:** with the toggle on and the default bindings, SUPER+SHIFT+2 on a base-10 monitor sends the window to workspace 2 on the base-0 monitor.

**Suggested change:** ship the binding change in the PR (for example, a Lua binding that calls the wrappers when the flag is on), or document the manual setup the feature requires.

### Disconnected monitors reset the desktop to slot 1 on reload

Bases are never removed by design ([`omarchy-monitor-base`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/13597029b25a90b70623ce82c1cc8aca9bdbad95/bin/omarchy-monitor-base#L19-L20)). [`omarchy-ensure-workspaces`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/13597029b25a90b70623ce82c1cc8aca9bdbad95/bin/omarchy-ensure-workspaces#L58-L84) runs after every config evaluation and `monitor.added`. It loops over all saved bases, dispatches focus to every missing workspace, then to workspace 1.

```text
Isolated run, synthetic hyprctl:
bases {eDP-1: 0, HDMI-A-1: 10}, only eDP-1 connected (workspaces 1-10 exist)
  -> dispatches focus 11, 12, ... 20, then 1
control: workspaces 1-20 exist -> no dispatch
```

Source-derived consequence: each missing workspace is created on the focused monitor, the `workspace.active` hook syncs every monitor to it, and the final dispatch leaves every monitor on slot 1. The switch helper loops over the same saved list.

**Impact:** for anyone whose saved bases include a display that is no longer connected (for example after one docking session), every reload, login and hotplug cycles through slots and leaves the desktop on slot 1. This became reachable in this commit, because the bases file was always empty before.

**Suggested change:** in both helpers, iterate only monitors currently reported by `hyprctl monitors -j`, and drop the unconditional return to workspace 1.

## New in this revision

### The bar can miss the first enable on a fresh setup

[`Workspaces.qml`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/13597029b25a90b70623ce82c1cc8aca9bdbad95/shell/plugins/bar/widgets/Workspaces.qml#L20-L40) watches `~/.local/state/omarchy/toggles/hypr` once, when the widget is created. Quickshell's `FileView` also watches the parent directory, but Qt cannot watch a path that does not exist. If neither `toggles/hypr` nor `toggles` exists at bar startup, nothing is watched. `omarchy-hyprland-toggle` creates them later, and the bar is not notified. Source-derived. Nothing under `install/` or `migrations/` creates these directories, so a fresh install where no toggle has been used yet is affected.

**Impact:** Hyprland runs in global mode while the bar keeps the local mapping until the shell restarts. Secondary monitors' workspaces do not light a button, and bar clicks go to raw workspace N.

**Suggested change:** have the toggle command nudge the shell over IPC, as `omarchy-toggle-bar` does for the bar-off flag, or create `toggles/hypr` during install or in a migration.

### The move helper's fallback is now unreachable

This commit added `set -euo pipefail` ([line 12](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/13597029b25a90b70623ce82c1cc8aca9bdbad95/bin/omarchy-hyprland-workspace-global-move-window#L12)). When the focused monitor is missing from the bases map, the embedded Python exits 1 and `TARGET_WS=$(...)` ends the script before the [raw-slot fallback](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/13597029b25a90b70623ce82c1cc8aca9bdbad95/bin/omarchy-hyprland-workspace-global-move-window#L73-L75) runs. Isolated run: bases `{eDP-1: 0}`, focused `HDMI-A-1`, so the helper exits 1 with no move. At `caff3e03ef34` it moved the window to `"2"`.

**Impact:** a monitor not yet in the map gets no move at all. The Lua allocator normally keeps connected monitors in the map, so this is an edge case.

**Suggested change:** `if ! TARGET_WS=$(...); then` around the assignment, with the fallback inside.

### Workspace IDs above 99 stop syncing

The Lua hook ignores workspace IDs above 99 ([`workspace-global.lua:232`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/13597029b25a90b70623ce82c1cc8aca9bdbad95/default/hypr/toggles/workspace-global.lua#L232)), and the bar maps them to no slot ([`Workspaces.qml:52`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/13597029b25a90b70623ce82c1cc8aca9bdbad95/shell/plugins/bar/widgets/Workspaces.qml#L52)). The allocators have no cap and never free bases, so the tenth distinct monitor name gets base 90, and later names start at 100. Source-derived.

**Impact:** on those monitors, some or all slots do not sync other monitors and show no focus or occupancy in the bar. Physical connectors rarely reach ten names. Unnamed headless outputs get a new `HEADLESS-n` name each time, so a virtual-display workflow can reach this, and the state is permanent.

**Suggested change:** derive the slot from the bases map instead of a fixed `99` bound, or skip or reuse bases for headless outputs.

**Test-only failures:** these do not affect runtime behavior. The new [`monitor-base-test.sh`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/13597029b25a90b70623ce82c1cc8aca9bdbad95/test/shell.d/monitor-base-test.sh#L73-L82) fails at this head. Its last case expects `sync` to print persisted bases when `hyprctl` fails, but `sync` exits 1 there, so the file aborts after 8 of 9 checks. Separately, `bin-style-test.sh` rejects the raw `command -v hyprctl` at [`omarchy-monitor-base:119`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/13597029b25a90b70623ce82c1cc8aca9bdbad95/bin/omarchy-monitor-base#L119); that has failed since `caff3e03ef34`. Using `omarchy-cmd-missing` or dropping the check fixes it. `omarchy-hyprland-workspace-global-move-window` also lacks `# omarchy:hidden=true`.

**Optional test improvement:** the switch and move tests replace the global helpers with stubs and pass unchanged at `caff3e03ef34`, where the move helper still sent windows to the wrong workspace. Running the real move helper against a stub `hyprctl` with a focused non-base-0 monitor would catch that regression.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** pinned-source inspection of `13597029b25a` against `caff3e03ef34` and base, with Hyprland 0.56.2, hyprutils, Quickshell and Qt source. Isolated command runs used a synthetic `hyprctl` and a stub Hyprland Lua API. They covered the allocator, the move helper, `omarchy-ensure-workspaces`, the Lua module and the repository tests named above. No native Hyprland, bar rendering, multi-monitor, hotplug or reload-timing test was run. Focus, bar-watch and workspace-bound results are source-derived or modelled.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, with independent Opus 5.5 Xhigh and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical assessments of this revision and targeted cross-checks of claims first raised by only one reviewer. Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
